title: Linux Inode Exhaustion (0 Inodes Available)
symptom: Application encounters 'No space left on device', but `df -h` shows gigabytes of free disk capacity.
initial_observations: touch /tmp/testfile fails with 'No space left on device'.
environment: Linux server hosting web service with extensive temporary or session files.

possible_causes.cause: Millions of tiny session or temporary files accumulated in /tmp, /var/spool, or /var/lib/php/sessions
possible_causes.evidence_needed: df -i shows IUse% at 100%; directory contains hundreds of thousands of entries.
possible_causes.remediation: Clean accumulated orphan session files using find with -delete, and configure cron cleanup job.

investigation_steps.title: Check Inode Consumption Across Filesystems
investigation_steps.explanation: Measure inode usage percentage (IUse%) rather than block capacity.

investigation_steps.title: Locate Directories with the Highest File Counts
investigation_steps.command: sudo find / -xdev -printf '%h\n' | sort | uniq -c | sort -k1 -n | tail -15
investigation_steps.explanation: Count file entries per directory across the filesystem.
investigation_steps.what_to_look_for: Directories containing hundreds of thousands of files.

verification: Run `df -i /` and confirm IFree > 0 and IUse% < 80%.
prevention: Set up automated tmpfiles.d or cron cleanup policies for session caches.
Monitor inode usage alongside disk block usage in CloudWatch.
